name: Kernel-Level Packet Fuzzer
problem: Network stacks are often tested with valid traffic, leaving edge-case vulnerabilities in TCP/IP parsing logic undiscovered.
pain: Lack of deterministic, stateful protocol fuzzer that can inject malformed packets into a local loopback interface.
solution: A C11 network fuzzer that crafts arbitrary Ethernet/IP/TCP frames, performs checksum manipulation, and monitors kernel-space socket state for crashes or hangs.
verification: Deterministic replay of failed test sequences; validation of packet integrity against RFC standards; automated detection of socket-level resource leaks.
major_features: Raw socket capture and injection interface
Checksum corruption and sequence number randomization
Stateful tracking of TCP connection lifecycle
Automated reproduction of crash-inducing packet sequences
Real-time packet capture and logging to pcap format
Configurable mutation rate and protocol segment selection
Deterministic test suite for kernel panic detection
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
